First, let's recall the graph of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14264109/assets/6eb672fe024f024f20c7c3c80947d1b47bade8f998e705d6f411ae3f298ecde2.png)

Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. If we rotate the graph ${180}^{∘}$ around the origin, we get the same picture. This means that $\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ is an *odd* function, and we have

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x)=-\operatorname{cot}⁡x.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cot}⁡(-x) & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡x \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
